newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ireland, EU hope deal on currency pact next week.
newsitem.headline: Ireland, EU hope deal on currency pact next week.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton and European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Thursday they were hopeful that the EU's summit next week would agree a budget stability pact for Economic and Monetary Union.

"We hope we will be able to reach agreement on the stability pact in full," Bruton told a news conference after meeting Santer ahead of the European Council of EU heads of state and government on December 13-14 in Dublin.
Finance ministers will meet next Thursday with the intention of agreeing the final details of the pact linking the participants in the single currency -- the Euro -- which is to be launched in 1999.

Bruton and Santer were optimistic there would also be a final agreement on the legal framework for the Euro and on a new exchange mechanism between the countries that adopt the Euro and those that do not.
Bruton said he was aiming for a deal on all three issues in Dublin.
"(We) envisage an agreement on a package, because a package is much better in terms of the confidence that it gives," he said.
EU finance ministers have still to agree on a definition of "exceptional and temporary circumstances" under which EU states which adopt the Euro might exceed a three-percent budget deficit target.
